key_insight: VLA Foundry unifies language, vision, and action model training in a single open-source codebase, giving researchers end-to-end control from pretraining to action-expert fine-tuning. It supports both from‑scratch training and plug‑in of pretrained Hugging Face backbones to eliminate brittle, stitched pipelines.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation and incompatibility in VLA development where separate LLM/VLM/VLA stages are manually stitched together, hindering reproducibility, iteration speed, and end-to-end experimentation.
method: A shared, modular training stack that standardizes data, optimizer, and checkpointing across LLM, VLM, and action stages.
Unified pipelines that enable end-to-end runs or stage-wise workflows (language pretraining → vision alignment → action-expert fine-tuning).
Flexible backbone support: train from scratch or import Hugging Face pretrained models for rapid prototyping and transfer learning.
impact: Reduces engineering overhead and increases reproducibility for multimodal action research, enabling faster iteration and fairer comparisons of VLA methods across consistent training protocols.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing a single pipeline with three labeled stages (Language → Vision → Action) and toggles for "from-scratch" vs "pretrained" backbones.

paper_title: VLA Foundry: A Unified Framework for Training Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_authors: Jean Mercat, Sedrick Keh, Kushal Arora, Isabella Huang, Paarth Shah
